title: Most caring and gentle habit tracker ever
body:
I hate routine. I hate being forced to do the exact same things every day of my life. I feel like schedule ruins my freedom of everyday life. And I believe that it is so easy to forget about your real life if you devote too much time to the goals. But what if I still need an app to make my life better?

Well, after a week of using Fabulous here’s what I can say:
1. You start with really simple tasks. And I get it: you are hardly able to achieve some serious goals if you can’t manage drink water every morning. I was upset at first, as many of other people on the comments, but when I got the point everything suddenly started making so much sense. And most of these tasks are not restrictive but rather encouraging, they’re relatively simple but I get so much feedback from achieving them.

2. Fabulous says about the environment that makes it easier for you to follow the habits. And it creates this environment itself: the menu with audios (stretch, meditation, yoga, etc) really helps me, since I don’t need to look for other meditation/stretch instructions, though you are free to do so if you want to get another experience. But i think this is definitely perfect for a good start.

3. I’m not a fan of the whole challenges concept, but maybe in the future I’ll try it out. And I think this might be helpful for some other people who like competition and that sort of thing.

4. When the time comes you’re supposed to do a part of your routine, there’s a sort of screensaver with a nice picture and sound. You can use it as you like. For me, it really improves my eating habits and helps not to distract on social feeds or other things I usually do while eating. Small but still a nice feature.

5. I told in the beginning about forgetting about your life and your present because of the goals. Well, in Fabulous, the goals suggested by the journeys become an essential part of your everyday life, your present, and they make you feel present right here, in this moment.

6. But what’s most important for me is that they constantly tell you that you do it not for the goals, but to “show yourself some kindness” and care. And this concept I like very much. Also, they regularly remind you to celebrate even the smallest achievements. Oh, never in my life was I so happy after eating a tomato for the first time in a month.

As for cons:
1. I was really confused about the whole journeys/goals/challenges concept, and it would be easier if you showed us the interface and everything the the app can do, and showed us how all of this actually works and how you can use it for maximum effectivity, in the beginning. For now, I’m still figuring it out.

2. I actually didn’t like the whole concept of fighting the “demons” (bad habits) since those appear as a coping mechanism in order to help you manage stress and other difficult stuff. The moment you realise this, stopping bad habits becomes much easier. Though I understand that fighting the demons might sound encouraging for some people and are a subjective author’s vision. And that’s fine, I was just surprised to see it in the app that talks about self care all the time.

3. Oh, and also that first water drinking point in the beginning that couldn’t be unchecked really confused me.

In overall, this app is awesome (should I’ve used the “Fabulous” pun?). Keep going guys, you’ve done a really great job so far. Wish you much inspiration and prosperity in both your lives and this project!

body:
Идиотский неудобный интерфейс. Логика работы самого приложения крайне странная: сперва говорят, мол, не так быстро - давай сначала воду пить с утра научимся; но тут же можно понаставить себе кучу заданий, выполнить их, тупо прокликав галочки, и тебя похвалят и переведут на следующий уровень.
Конечно же, апа постоянно напоминает о том, что неплохо бы купить подписку ;)
